policy_title: Reform Water Company Price Review Process
stated: The Conservative Party will reform the 'Price Review' regulatory process for water companies to move towards a more localised, catchment-based, and outcome-focused approach, strengthening sanctions for companies that fail to deliver.

source.quote: To deliver our ambitious plan for water beyond 2030, we will reform the ‘Price Review’ regulatory process for water companies. This will consider how we move to a more localised catchment-based and outcome-focussed approach, that better utilises nature-based solutions and further strengthens sanctions for water companies that fail to deliver for the public, coasts and rivers.

bearing_set.reason: A catchment-based, outcome-focused price review directly targets water quality management, and stronger sanctions for non-delivery materially affects environmental performance of water companies — water quality is a core O6 indicator.

The Price Review process is the mechanism that sets allowed water company revenues and hence household water bills; reforming it can materially move what households pay for an essential utility, affecting disposable income and the bills component of the cost-of-living basket.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O6 is the primary design target (water quality/nature); O2 is an unavoidable structural effect because the Price Review is literally the bill-setting process. A plausible tradeoff runs between them — tougher environmental outcomes may require higher capital investment passed through to bills, so the two outcomes can pull in opposite directions.
